LOOK_AT.say: A pocket watch on a nail in the ridgepole, so the whole camp can see the time.

then.speaker: thad
then.line: He turns, slowly, to the man behind the plank. The man behind the plank is beaming.

then.speaker: gulch_deacon
then.line: Grubb! You came all this way. Was the claim not to your liking?

then: The claim contains a raccoon and an opinion.

then.speaker: gulch_deacon
then.line: It contained a raccoon when I sold it. You bought the whole thing.

then.speaker: gulch_deacon
then.line: For the heat, son. You'd never have known me.

LOOK_AT.say: An empty nail. Vessel took the watch with him. Tomorrow the camp will be on time, and won't know why.
My father's watch, keeping time for a camp full of strangers. Eleven minutes fast, as ever.
repeat: Every man here is eleven minutes early to everything, and none of them knows why. I know why.

LISTEN_TO.say: No ticking. The tent sounds a little lost.
Ticking, high up on the pole.
repeat: Ticking. It's the only thing in the camp in a hurry.
Ticking, steady, above all the talk.

PICK_UP.say: Vessel says it's the camp's now. The camp says it's Vessel's. Nobody says it's mine.

PICK_UP.say: It's on a nail above the keeper's head, and the keeper is watching me look at it.
PICK_UP.sceneLine: docs/109-fiddlers-gulch-lines.md::## THE GROG TENT · **PICK UP** — *before the find:* *before the find:*

LOOK_AT.say: In tune. Nobody here can play it, but now they can't play it properly.
A fiddle on a peg, with the bow tucked in the strings.
repeat: The pegs have slipped, all four. The strings hang like a wet line.
I could put it right in a minute. Nobody's asked. Nobody here asks for anything they can't buy.
then: Fiddler's Gulch, and nobody plays it.

LISTEN_TO.say: Quiet, and in tune. It's the best-kept thing in the camp now.
A string buzzing when the plank shakes. It's flat. They're all flat.
repeat: The E, sagging a good half-tone. It hurts a little.
Quiet, until someone leans on the plank. Then it moans.

LOOK_AT.say: Two barrels holding up the plank, and a third holding up the rule-keeper.
repeat: WHISKEY, says one. FLOUR, says the other. They've both got whiskey in.
I tapped one. Full. I tapped the other. Also full. A rich camp drinks from both ends.
A slow drip from a tap, into a cup kept under it.
A gurgle, low down. The flour is very wet.

overrides.OPEN: I reached for a tap. The keeper cleared his throat in a way that cost a pinch.

LOOK_AT.say: A plank across two barrels: the bar. Elbows have polished it to a shine.
repeat: A brass plate is screwed to it: GOLD ON THE PLANK. Even the furniture has rules.
I put my elbow on it. The keeper looked at my elbow until I took it off.

LISTEN_TO.say: Glasses set down, one at a time.
repeat: The plank creaking as a man leans.
A coin spinning on the wood, then lying still.

overrides.PICK_UP: It's the bar. You don't pick up a man's bar. Not here, and not with him watching.

LOOK_AT.say: Bottles along a shelf, with labels that promise France.
repeat: One says COGNAC. It was filled from the WHISKEY barrel. I watched.
The prices are chalked on the shelf, by the pinch. A pinch of what isn't in question.

LISTEN_TO.say: Glass clinking when the tent moves.
repeat: A bottle being uncorked by a man in no hurry.
Clink. Then a sigh from whoever paid.

overrides.PICK_UP: The prices are by the pinch, and I haven't got one. I put it back, carefully, while he watched.

exits.name: THE TENT FLAP

LOOK_AT.say: The flap, tied back, and the camp outside.
repeat: Daylight, and a hundred rich men who don't trust each other.
A man ducked in under it as I looked, already holding out his pinch.

LISTEN_TO.say: The river, out past the tents.
repeat: Wind snapping at the flap.
Canvas cracking in the wind, and shovels beyond.

overrides.CLOSE: I untied it. The whole tent looked at me. I tied it back.

PICK_UP.say: Not a man behind his own bar. That's how you end up underneath it.

PUSH.say: I leaned across the plank at him. He leaned back the same distance, smiling, like we'd done this before.

USE.say: He's working. Every man in here is using him, a pinch at a time.

LOOK_AT.say: Deke Vessel, without his mustache. I'd have known the mustache anywhere. That was the trouble.
repeat: He's selling whiskey to men who can pay for it, and he's never looked happier.
He winked at me just now, fondly. I'm a good memory to him.

LOOK_AT.say: The man behind the plank: clean-shaven, sunburnt, and very pleased with himself.
repeat: There's a pale stripe across his top lip, as if something used to live there.
He seems to know me. He hasn't said so. He hasn't said he doesn't, either.
Coins dropping into a box under the plank.
Chuckling. Possibly at me.

PICK_UP.say: Him and the barrel both? Not without a mule, and the mule's at the washout.

PUSH.say: Push a man off his barrel and he'd make a rule about it. Then he'd get it wrong, against me.

USE.say: He's the camp's rule book. I'd look something up, but the answer changes every time.

LOOK_AT.say: A big man on a barrel with a glass and a bag of pebbles. He keeps the camp's rules, from memory.
repeat: He's sure of every rule and wrong about most of them, and nobody's ever checked.
He wears a gold watch-chain with no watch on it. He tells the time by looking at the pole.
Muttering the rules under his breath, in a new order.
A long swallow, then a satisfied 'ah'.
